newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps- Aug gas oil up on cash support.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps- Aug gas oil up on cash support.

text.p: Singapore front month August gas oil swaps rose in thin trading at midday on Wednesday after fresh physical buying emerged late Tuesday, traders said.
"I think the August gas oil went up because of the buying that came out yesterday," one trader said.
August gas oil was last quoted at $23.15/$23.30, up from Monday's $22.95/$23.05.
The hike to August values was not mirrored in September which was largely unchanged from Tuesday at $23.75/$23.90.
As a result the August/September spread which traded on Tuesday at minus 75 cents is now valued at about minus 60 cents, brokers said.
Traders said the steady September prices were reflective of the unchanged market fundamentals.
On Tuesday a 150,000-barrel cargo traded at $22.90 per barrel free-on-board Singapore basis for August 22-29 lifting, up 40 cents from Monday's traded level.

Traders said the deal indicated renewed buying interest from traders in the Singapore spot market despite poor regional demand where India only bought a meagre 90,000 tonnes of diesel for September arrival.
Other regional buyers such as China and Indonesia are also only purchasing small amounts, they said.
The jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade rose despite the rising outright gas oil swaps values as buyers entered the market in anticipation of fresh jet fuel demand as players stock up for the winter.
August regrade was last quoted at 70/90 cents compared to Tuesday's 50/70 cents, brokers said.
Fuel oil extended its early week rally on strong bunker demand and tight supplies.
August and September swaps were last quoted at $103.00/$104.00 per tonne, from Tuesday's $102.50/$103.00, brokes said.
